name: Indegene Ltd
title: Indegene Ltd - 544172 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Indegene Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR11,223 million, with EBITDA margin at 16.7% and a 19%+ target for Q4.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR11,223 million, up 39.5% YoY and 5.6% QoQ in INR, the fifth straight quarter of more than 5% QoQ INR growth. EBITDA was INR1,873 million at a 16.7% margin, absorbing about 150 bps from the annual wage hike, which productivity and favourable exchange rates largely offset. PAT rose 10% YoY to INR1,123 million, though a sharp fall in interest income (down 44% QoQ) weighed below EBITDA. Management reiterated a quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 and said H2 would be stronger than H1, while the largest client dipped slightly and the $10 million outcome-based contract is expected to peak in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +39.5% YoY, +5.6% QoQ in INR; +27.5% YoY and +4.4% QoQ in USD

financial_highlights.metric: Net DSO (net of unearned and unbilled revenue)

financial_highlights.change: Up from about US$69,000 a year ago

segments.name: Enterprise Commercial
segments.commentary: Contributed about 71% of revenue; deal wins skewed to Commercial and management expects Commercial to outgrow Medical over the next few quarters.

segments.name: Enterprise Medical
segments.commentary: Contributed about 25% of revenue; growth was weaker this quarter against a strong prior base, though $2 million-plus Medical deals were closed.

segments.name: Others (incl. Clinical)
segments.commentary: About 4% of revenue; growth lifted by a large Clinical deal that ramped in August and will annualise in Q3.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: North America 74%, Europe 23%, rest of world 3% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: Quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 FY27, unchanged; management says H2 margin growth should outpace revenue growth as Q4 exits.
Organic growth for FY27 expected to be better than FY26; management says FY27 will be organically stronger than last year and H2 stronger than H1.
Wage hike is fully in the base; productivity, workforce transformation and operating leverage expected to add to EBITDA in Q3 and more in Q4.

Amortisation charge to decline from Q3 onward; yields expected to rise with higher rates and a shift to held-to-maturity instruments. Together these add about 90-95 bps to PBT, helping PAT margin expand faster than EBITDA margin.
Management does not give formal or quarter-on-quarter guidance.
BioPharm earnout: second tranche expected close to maximum payout, already fully provided on the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Revenue per employee rising as GenAI platforms lift output and more work is priced on output or outcomes rather than time spent.
Tectonic run rate grew from about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter; contracts now exceed $2 million a quarter.
Approximately 75% of the next two quarters' forex exposure is already hedged.
Dedicated tech partnership team in the US and India to work with frontier model and other technology companies.
demand_pricing: Q2 deal wins: 9 deals with ACV around $1 million or more, including one $5 million-plus win (expansion of the top-5 client's content migration outside the US), one $3-5 million global content factory win with a top-20 pharma, and one win with a top-30 pharma replacing an incumbent.
Four further deals in the $1-3 million range, split evenly between Enterprise Commercial and Enterprise Medical; Tectonic extended to Canada, the first market outside Europe.
Top 5 accounts grew 9.2% QoQ in INR; top 20 grew about 6.7% QoQ. Active clients 107 (31 more YoY); clients above $1 million rose to 59 from 54; clients above $10 million at 13.
Largest client is 7.8% of revenue; top 10 clients are 49%. This client's revenue eased as Tectonic ramps slowly, and one customer dropped from the $25 million-plus cohort to just below it.
Most Q2 wins were output- or outcome-based rather than FTE-based. The company is converting FTE contracts to hybrid contracts at renewal.
A $10 million ACV outcome-based contract (calendar-year threshold) recognised only a small amount in Q2; the bulk is expected in H2, with a true-up in Q4 after customer confirmation in Feb/Mar.
BioPharm: cost synergies of about $1.5 million a year reinvested in expanding BioPharm's go-to-market team from 3 to 9. Transition services closed by end-February, ahead of the March target.
Management sees competition from agencies and CROs, not IT services firms, in the deals it pursues.

qa_highlights.question: What are Tectonic run rates and contract values?
qa_highlights.answer: Tectonic grew from about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter; contracts have crossed $2 million a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the largest client's ramp slower while scope grows, and how is Tectonic ROI measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to central teams driving centralisation while local brand teams stay decentralised; it expects this to play out over time. Tectonic is not measured standalone; ROI will be judged across the full upstream value chain.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on outcome-based revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a cap. Most Q2 wins were output- or outcome-based, and FTE contracts are being converted to hybrid models at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $10 million outcome-based deal in revenue yet, and when will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: A small amount was recognised in Q2; most is ahead, with H2 the main recognition period and Q4 the peak after the true-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin walk from 16.7% toward 18-19%?
qa_highlights.answer: Productivity and workforce transformation added about 85 bps in Q2 QoQ; favourable FX and operating leverage should keep helping in Q3 and Q4, with the $10 million contract adding more in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the largest client's dip temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; the client's $5 million-plus win is ramping, and management expects it back above $25 million in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect H2 to be stronger than Q2 momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide quarterly, but expects FY27 organic growth above FY26 and H2 stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the frontier model AI a threat, and how do TCS-type IT players affect competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see frontier labs as a threat and is partnering with them; it sees little IT services competition in the Commercial and Medical deals it pursues.

risks_watch: Largest client (7.8% of revenue) revenue eased QoQ; Tectonic ramp is slow and the client's central and local teams are not yet aligned.
A top client slipped below the $25 million-plus cohort; recovery depends on the $5 million-plus deal ramping over 2-3 quarters.
The $10 million outcome-based contract's revenue and margin benefit depends on meeting a full-year threshold, with the true-up in Q4 after February-March confirmation.
DSO rose to 69 days and unbilled revenue increased; management expects normalisation in Q3-Q4.
Interest income fell 44% QoQ on mark-to-market losses; recovery depends on yields rising as expected.
Medical segment growth lagging Commercial; the company is still investing in Medical.
Frontier AI labs moving into pharma drug discovery and content; management views this as a partnering opportunity rather than a threat.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, deal wins and H2 margin recovery, but openly cautious on near-term client ramp timing, which management describes as non-linear and dependent on customer change management. Management declined to quantify outcome-based revenue caps or give quarterly guidance.
key_quotes: Revenues came in at INR11,223 million, up 39.5% year-on-year and 5.6% sequentially.
We continue on the path to quarterly EBITDA margins of 19% plus by the fourth quarter of this year.
We don't see that as a threat to our model of working.
Most of the technology companies will have to partner with companies like us.

growth.why: Management reiterated a 19%+ quarterly EBITDA margin by Q4 FY27 and said FY27 organic growth will beat FY26 with H2 stronger than H1, backed by specific wins (nine ~$1M+ ACV deals, a $10M outcome-based contract peaking in Q4) but no company-added capacity and no formal revenue growth figure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated a quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 FY27 from 16.7% in Q2, with productivity adding about 85 bps QoQ in Q2 and PAT margin helped by about 90-95 bps from lower amortisation and higher yields.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects FY27 organic growth above FY26 and H2 stronger than H1, backed by nine ~$1M+ ACV deals in Q2 and a $10M outcome-based contract peaking in Q4, though no formal revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held its 19%+ quarterly EBITDA margin and FY27 organic growth above FY26 guidance, with a $5M+ win and $10M contract ramping, but gave no formal or quarterly guidance to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Largest client (7.8% of revenue) eased QoQ and a top client slipped below the $25M cohort, while DSO rose to 69 days and the $10M contract's true-up depends on Feb-Mar confirmation.

rows.label: $10M outcome-based contract peaks in Q4
rows.why: A small amount was recognised in Q2 and the bulk is expected in H2, with a Q4 true-up after customer confirmation in Feb/Mar.

rows.label: Tectonic ramp and run-rate growth
rows.why: Tectonic run rate rose from about $1M a quarter to $1.7M this quarter, contracts now exceed $2M a quarter, and it extended to Canada, the first market outside Europe.

rows.label: Largest client recovery above $25M
rows.why: Management expects the client back above $25M in 2-3 quarters as a $5M-plus win ramps, but the ramp is described as non-linear.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 margin recovery, deal wins and the $10M contract, but cautious on the largest client's slow ramp and DSO; analysts pushed on outcome-based revenue caps and near-term client ramp timing, which management declined to quantify.
